Information since the June meeting indicates continued labor-market strengthening and moderate growth, while 12-month inflation remains below the 2 percent objective and market-based inflation compensation is low, consistent with anchored expectations. Incorporating SLOOS: banks reported weakened loan demand across CRE (including construction, land development, and multifamily) and consumer credit (auto and credit cards), with tighter standards for consumer/auto/credit cards; demand was roughly unchanged for nonfarm nonresidential loans. By contrast, banks eased standards for residential real estate (including jumbo, QM, and GSE mortgages) and kept standards roughly unchanged for home-purchase loans and HELOCs. Foreign banks reported tighter standards for C&I and CRE, with some strength in CRE loan demand. This credit mix implies headwinds for consumer and CRE activity, partially offset by easier mortgage credit, reinforcing a gradual, accommodative policy path with forward guidance and balance-sheet normalization rather than aggressive near-term hikes. Net: slightly less positive than previously assessed.
